newsitem.title: USA: Europe-U.S. wide apart on environment - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Europe-U.S. wide apart on environment - Chirac.

text.p: European countries have widely different views from the United States on measures to protect the environment, French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday following talks among the Group of Seven wealthy nations.

European countries had been pressing for action to reduce carbon dioxide and other gases by 15 percent by the year 2010, officials said. They also wanted action on preventing deforestatation but met with little success on either issue.
"There is a real divergence of views between, on one hand the Europeans and on the other the Americans -- not Canada, the United States," Chirac told a news conference.
The Group of Seven comprises the United States, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy, France and Britain.
Failure to make progress on environmental issues came ahead of a United Nations Earth Summit in New York on Monday meant to review attempts for concerted worldwide action on the environment.
